questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: According to Genesis, God created the world in a period of
options: six days, resting on the seventh
seven days, resting on the eighth
questions.explanation: Genesis 1 records that God completed creation in six days and rested on the seventh, establishing the pattern for the Sabbath.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the Genesis creation account, human beings are described as being made
options: in the image and likeness of God
questions.explanation: Genesis 1:26-27 states that God created humankind in His own image, giving humans a unique status among creation.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the second creation account (Genesis 2), God formed the first man from
options: the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into him
water from the Garden of Eden
a rib taken from an animal
questions.explanation: Genesis 2:7 describes God forming man from dust and breathing life into him, making him a living being.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: According to Genesis 2, God created the first woman from
options: a rib taken from an animal
the dust of the ground directly
a rib taken from the man
questions.explanation: Genesis 2:21-22 describes God creating the woman from one of Adam's ribs while he slept.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The tree in the Garden of Eden from which Adam and Eve were forbidden to eat is called
options: the tree of the knowledge of good and evil
questions.explanation: Genesis 2:17 records God's command forbidding Adam from eating the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the temptation narrative, the serpent tempted Eve by suggesting that eating the forbidden fruit would
options: cause immediate death with no other effect
make her and Adam like God, knowing good and evil
questions.explanation: Genesis 3:5 records the serpent's claim that eating the fruit would open their eyes and make them like God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: As a direct consequence of the Fall, God pronounced that the woman would experience
options: increased pain in childbirth and be ruled over by her husband
questions.explanation: Genesis 3:16 records God's pronouncement of increased pain in childbirth and the woman's relationship to her husband as consequences of the Fall.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: As a consequence of the Fall, God cursed the ground so that man would
options: toil and labour painfully to produce food from it
never need to work the land again
questions.explanation: Genesis 3:17-19 describes the ground being cursed, requiring man to labour painfully for his food, 'by the sweat of your brow'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Following the Fall, Adam and Eve were ultimately
options: driven out of the Garden of Eden
given greater authority over the garden
questions.explanation: Genesis 3:23-24 describes God expelling Adam and Eve from Eden, with cherubim placed to guard the way back to the tree of life.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: God's call to Abraham, recorded in Genesis 12, required him to
options: leave his country and his father's household for a land God would show him
remain permanently in Ur of the Chaldees
build the first temple in Jerusalem
lead the Israelites out of Egypt
questions.explanation: Genesis 12:1 records God's call for Abraham to leave his homeland and kindred for an unspecified land God would reveal to him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: As part of God's covenant with Abraham, God promised that
options: Abraham's descendants would remain in Egypt forever
Abraham would become the father of a great nation and all families of the earth would be blessed through him
Abraham would never have any descendants
Abraham would be the last of the patriarchs
questions.explanation: Genesis 12:2-3 records God's covenant promise to make Abraham a great nation and a source of blessing to all peoples.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The sign of the covenant God gave to Abraham, to be practised by every male descendant, was
questions.explanation: Genesis 17 records circumcision as the physical sign of the covenant between God and Abraham's descendants.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: God called Moses to lead the Israelites out of Egypt while Moses was tending sheep and encountered God through
options: an angel appearing at the Red Sea
a burning bush that was not consumed
questions.explanation: Exodus 3 records God calling Moses through a bush that burned without being consumed, on Mount Horeb.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The renewal of God's covenant with Israel, including the giving of the Ten Commandments, took place at
questions.explanation: Exodus 19-20 records God renewing His covenant with Israel and giving the Ten Commandments at Mount Sinai.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Joseph rose to become a powerful leader in Egypt mainly because he
options: was the eldest of Jacob's sons
led a military conquest of Egypt
correctly interpreted Pharaoh's dreams and wisely managed the famine preparations
questions.explanation: Genesis 41 records Joseph interpreting Pharaoh's dreams about the coming famine and being placed in charge of Egypt's preparations.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Joseph's brothers originally sold him into slavery mainly out of
options: a desire to protect him from Pharaoh
jealousy over their father's favouritism and Joseph's dreams
questions.explanation: Genesis 37 records the brothers' jealousy over Jacob's favouritism toward Joseph and his dreams of ruling over them.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Under Moses' leadership, the Israelites' escape from bondage in Egypt is known as the
questions.explanation: The Exodus refers to the departure of the Israelites from slavery in Egypt under Moses' leadership.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: During the Exodus, the Israelites crossed the Red Sea after God
options: caused the sea to disappear permanently
parted the waters, allowing them to pass through on dry ground
questions.explanation: Exodus 14 records God parting the Red Sea, allowing the Israelites to cross on dry ground while the pursuing Egyptian army was later drowned.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: After Moses' death, the leader who succeeded him and led Israel into the land of Canaan was
questions.explanation: Joshua succeeded Moses as leader of Israel, guiding the people into Canaan, including the conquest of Jericho.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The famous city whose walls fell after the Israelites marched around it under Joshua's leadership was
questions.explanation: Joshua 6 recounts the fall of Jericho's walls after the Israelites marched around the city as instructed by God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Israelites' demand for a king, presented to the prophet Samuel, was partly motivated by their desire to
options: be like other surrounding nations that had kings
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 8 records the elders' request for a king so that Israel could be governed like the surrounding nations.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The first king of Israel, anointed by the prophet Samuel, was
questions.explanation: Saul, from the tribe of Benjamin, was anointed by Samuel as Israel's first king.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: King Saul was ultimately rejected by God mainly because of his
options: disobedience, including offering an unlawful sacrifice and sparing the Amalekites against God's command
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 13 and 15 record Saul's disobedience in offering a sacrifice reserved for Samuel and failing to fully destroy the Amalekites as commanded, leading to his rejection.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: David was chosen and anointed by Samuel to succeed Saul while David was still
options: a priest serving in the temple
a young shepherd tending his father's sheep
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 16 describes Samuel anointing David, the youngest son of Jesse, while he was still tending sheep.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: David's grave sin involving Bathsheba included
options: committing adultery with her and arranging the death of her husband Uriah
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 11 recounts David's adultery with Bathsheba and his plot to have her husband Uriah killed in battle to cover it up.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: David's genuine repentance for his sin with Bathsheba came after he was confronted by the prophet
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12 records the prophet Nathan confronting David with a parable that led him to acknowledge and repent of his sin.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: King Solomon, David's son and successor, is best known in scripture for his exceptional
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3 records God granting Solomon extraordinary wisdom in response to his humble request, exemplified in his famous judgement between two women.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Despite his wisdom and wealth, Solomon's downfall (apostasy) came about mainly through
options: an invasion by a foreign army
his many foreign wives turning his heart toward idol worship
a famine that destroyed his kingdom
his refusal to build the temple
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11 records how Solomon's many foreign wives led him to worship other gods, provoking God's anger.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: After Solomon's death, the kingdom of Israel was divided mainly due to a dispute between
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12 records the kingdom splitting into Israel (north) under Jeroboam and Judah (south) under Rehoboam, following harsh policies by Rehoboam.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: King Ahab of Israel provoked significant religious tension mainly through his support for the worship of
options: Baal, encouraged by his wife Jezebel
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 16 and 18 describe Ahab's promotion of Baal worship, heavily influenced by his wife Jezebel, which set the stage for conflict with Elijah.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Elijah's dramatic contest with the prophets of Baal took place on
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18 records Elijah's contest with 450 prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel, which demonstrated Yahweh's supremacy through fire from heaven.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The prophet Amos is especially known for his message condemning
options: social injustice and the oppression of the poor
questions.explanation: Amos's prophecies strongly denounce the exploitation of the poor and the social injustices prevalent in Israel.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The prophet Hosea's own troubled marriage was used symbolically in his prophecy to represent
options: the political alliance between Israel and Judah
the wealth of the Israelite nation
Israel's unfaithfulness to God despite God's persistent love
questions.explanation: Hosea's marriage to Gomer symbolically portrayed Israel's spiritual unfaithfulness (idolatry) and God's enduring, forgiving love.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Babylonian exile refers to the period when
options: the people of Judah were forcibly taken into captivity in Babylon
questions.explanation: The Babylonian exile followed the fall of Jerusalem, with many Judeans forcibly deported to live in Babylon.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The prophet who ministered in Jerusalem before and during its fall to Babylon, often called the 'weeping prophet', was
questions.explanation: Jeremiah prophesied of Jerusalem's coming judgement and is traditionally known as the 'weeping prophet' for his laments over the city's fate.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The prophet who ministered among the exiles in Babylon, known for symbolic visions such as the valley of dry bones, was
questions.explanation: Ezekiel prophesied among the Babylonian exiles, using vivid symbolic visions, including the famous vision of the valley of dry bones representing Israel's restoration.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Persian-appointed leader who led the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls after the exile was
questions.explanation: Nehemiah, serving as governor, organised and oversaw the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls despite strong local opposition.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The priest and scribe who led religious reforms and the reading of the Law after the exile was
questions.explanation: Ezra led religious and social reforms among the returned exiles, notably through the public reading and teaching of the Law.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The covenant God made with Abraham was later renewed and expanded with the whole nation of Israel at Sinai, primarily through the giving of
questions.explanation: The Sinai covenant, centred on the Ten Commandments and broader Law, formalised Israel's relationship with God as His chosen people.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: A key lesson drawn from the story of Joseph and his brothers is that
options: leadership should always be inherited by the eldest son
God can turn even evil intentions into good outcomes
family betrayal always leads to permanent ruin
questions.explanation: Genesis 50:20 records Joseph's own reflection that what his brothers meant for evil, God used for good, to save many lives.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The angel who announced to Zechariah that his wife Elizabeth would bear a son, John the Baptist, was
questions.explanation: Luke 1 records the angel Gabriel appearing to Zechariah in the temple to announce the birth of John the Baptist.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The angel Gabriel announced to Mary that she would conceive and bear a son through
options: a natural marriage to Joseph beforehand
the power of the Holy Spirit, while remaining a virgin
a vision given to Joseph alone
questions.explanation: Luke 1:26-38 records the angel Gabriel's announcement to Mary that she would conceive by the Holy Spirit while still a virgin.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: John the Baptist's ministry mainly involved
options: writing one of the four Gospels
leading a political rebellion against Rome
preaching repentance and baptising people in the Jordan River
questions.explanation: John the Baptist called people to repentance and baptised them in the Jordan River, preparing the way for Jesus' ministry.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: At Jesus' baptism by John in the Jordan River, a voice from heaven declared Him to be
options: God's beloved Son, with whom He was well pleased
questions.explanation: At Jesus' baptism, a voice from heaven affirmed Him as God's beloved Son, while the Holy Spirit descended like a dove.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Following His baptism, Jesus was led into the wilderness where He was
options: crowned as king by the disciples
tempted by the devil for forty days
questions.explanation: Matthew 4 and Luke 4 record Jesus being led by the Spirit into the wilderness, where He fasted forty days and was tempted by the devil.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: During His temptation in the wilderness, Jesus resisted the devil's suggestions mainly by
options: calling on the angels for military help
negotiating a compromise with the devil
questions.explanation: In each temptation, Jesus responded by quoting relevant passages from the Hebrew scriptures to refute the devil's suggestions.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Among the first disciples Jesus called to follow Him were the fishermen brothers
options: James the son of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus
questions.explanation: Matthew 4 and Mark 1 record Jesus calling Simon Peter and his brother Andrew, who were fishermen, to follow Him and become 'fishers of men'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Sermon on the Mount begins with a series of blessings known as the
questions.explanation: Matthew 5 opens the Sermon on the Mount with the Beatitudes, a series of blessings pronounced on those with particular qualities and circumstances.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus described His followers as the 'salt of the earth' and the 'light of the world' to teach that they should
options: influence and positively affect the world around them
focus only on their personal spiritual growth
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:13-16 uses the images of salt and light to teach that believers should have a visible, beneficial influence on the wider world.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus' teaching on forgiveness emphasised that His followers should
options: forgive others so that they too may be forgiven by God
seek revenge against those who wrong them
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:14-15 records Jesus teaching that God's forgiveness of us is linked to our willingness to forgive others.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the Parable of the Sower, seed that fell on good soil represents
options: those who reject the word immediately
those who hear the word, understand it, and produce a fruitful harvest
those who never hear the word at all
those who hear the word but are choked by worldly worries
questions.explanation: Matthew 13 interprets the seed on good soil as representing people who truly hear, understand, and act fruitfully on God's word.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the Parable of the Mustard Seed, Jesus compared the Kingdom of God to a seed that
options: is planted only in barren soil
starts very small but grows into a large plant
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:31-32 uses the mustard seed to illustrate how the Kingdom of God, though starting small, grows to great significance.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son, the father's reaction upon his younger son's return demonstrates
options: permanent rejection of the wayward son
questions.explanation: Luke 15 records the father running to embrace his returning son, celebrating his return rather than condemning his past mistakes.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan, the person who ultimately proved to be a true neighbour to the injured man was
options: the Levite who also passed by
the innkeeper who was paid to help
the priest who passed by first
the Samaritan, despite being from a group despised by the Jews
questions.explanation: Luke 10 records that it was the Samaritan, not the priest or Levite, who showed true compassion and neighbourly love to the injured traveller.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Among Jesus' miracles demonstrating power over nature, He famously calmed a storm by
options: asking His disciples to row harder
waiting for the storm to end on its own
praying quietly until it passed naturally
rebuking the wind and the waves, bringing sudden calm
questions.explanation: Mark 4 records Jesus rebuking the storm with a word, immediately bringing calm and amazing His disciples.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the miracle of feeding the five thousand, Jesus multiplied a small amount of food consisting of
questions.explanation: All four Gospels record Jesus miraculously feeding a crowd of five thousand with just five loaves and two fish.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Among Jesus' miracles demonstrating power over sickness, He healed a paralysed man after his friends
options: left him at the town gate
brought him to John the Baptist instead
lowered him through a hole in the roof to reach Jesus
carried him to the temple for a sacrifice
questions.explanation: Mark 2 records the paralysed man's friends removing part of a roof to lower him down to Jesus through the crowded house.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus healed the servant of a Roman centurion after the centurion expressed
options: great faith, believing Jesus could heal with only a word from a distance
a demand that Jesus visit in person
a request for payment in exchange
questions.explanation: Matthew 8 records Jesus praising the centurion's exceptional faith, as he believed Jesus' word alone was sufficient to heal his servant remotely.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Among Jesus' miracles demonstrating power over death, He raised His close friend Lazarus after Lazarus had been
options: dead for only a few hours
dead and in the tomb for four days
questions.explanation: John 11 records Jesus raising Lazarus after four days in the tomb, a powerful demonstration of His authority over death.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus also raised from death the daughter of a synagogue official named
questions.explanation: Mark 5 and Luke 8 record Jesus raising the daughter of Jairus, a synagogue leader, after she had died.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: At the Last Supper, Jesus instituted what Christians commemorate as
questions.explanation: During the Last Supper, Jesus shared bread and wine with His disciples, establishing what became the Christian sacrament of Holy Communion.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus was betrayed to the religious authorities by one of His own twelve disciples, named
questions.explanation: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus to the chief priests for thirty pieces of silver, leading to His arrest.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus was tried before the Jewish religious council known as the
questions.explanation: Jesus was brought before the Sanhedrin, the supreme Jewish religious and legal council, on charges of blasphemy.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: After His trial before the Sanhedrin, Jesus was brought before the Roman governor for judgement, who was
questions.explanation: Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor of Judea, presided over Jesus' civil trial before authorising the crucifixion.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: According to the Gospels, Jesus was crucified at a place called
questions.explanation: Jesus was crucified at Golgotha, meaning 'Place of the Skull', just outside Jerusalem.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: According to the Gospels, Jesus rose from the dead on the
questions.explanation: The Gospels record Jesus rising on the third day after His crucifixion, fulfilling His own predictions.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: After His resurrection, Jesus appeared to His disciples over a period of
questions.explanation: Acts 1:3 records that Jesus appeared to His disciples over forty days after His resurrection, teaching them about the Kingdom of God before ascending.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus' ascension into heaven, witnessed by His disciples, took place at
questions.explanation: Acts 1 records Jesus ascending to heaven from the Mount of Olives in the presence of His disciples.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The dramatic outpouring of the Holy Spirit upon the early believers, marking the birth of the Church, occurred at
questions.explanation: Acts 2 records the Holy Spirit descending upon the disciples at Pentecost, empowering them to preach boldly in various languages.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The early Christian believers in Jerusalem, as described in Acts, were known for
options: sharing their possessions and living in close communal fellowship
questions.explanation: Acts 2:44-47 describes the early believers holding property in common and meeting together regularly in fellowship, prayer, and the breaking of bread.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The seven men appointed in Acts 6 to oversee the daily distribution of food to widows are commonly referred to as
questions.explanation: Acts 6 records the appointment of seven men, including Stephen, to manage the practical needs of the growing Jerusalem church, seen as the origin of the diaconate.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Stephen, one of the seven appointed to serve the early church, became the first Christian to
questions.explanation: Acts 7 records Stephen being stoned to death after his powerful defence of the Christian faith before the Sanhedrin, making him the first Christian martyr.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Saul of Tarsus, later known as Paul, was dramatically converted to Christianity while
options: fishing on the Sea of Galilee
worshipping in the temple in Jerusalem
travelling to Damascus to persecute Christians
questions.explanation: Acts 9 records Saul's dramatic encounter with the risen Christ on the road to Damascus, leading to his conversion and later missionary work as Paul.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Paul's missionary journeys, recorded in Acts, were primarily aimed at
options: spreading the Gospel and establishing churches across the Roman world
conquering territory for the Roman Empire
translating the Hebrew scriptures into Greek
questions.explanation: Paul undertook extensive missionary journeys to preach the Gospel and establish Christian communities throughout Asia Minor, Greece, and beyond.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Jerusalem Council, described in Acts 15, was convened mainly to decide
options: whether Gentile converts needed to observe Jewish law, such as circumcision
where the next temple should be built
how to distribute food to widows
questions.explanation: Acts 15 records the Jerusalem Council addressing the dispute over whether Gentile believers must follow Jewish customs like circumcision to be saved.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Before ascending to heaven, Jesus gave His disciples what is commonly known as the Great Commission, instructing them to
options: go and make disciples of all nations, baptising and teaching them
focus only on rebuilding the temple
questions.explanation: Matthew 28:19-20 records Jesus commissioning His disciples to spread the Gospel to all nations, baptising and teaching obedience to His commands.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The replacement chosen by the apostles to take the place of Judas Iscariot among the twelve was
questions.explanation: Acts 1 records the apostles casting lots to choose Matthias as a replacement for Judas among the twelve.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: On the day of Pentecost, the crowd in Jerusalem was amazed because the disciples, filled with the Holy Spirit, were
options: speaking in other languages, understood by people from many nations
reading from the Torah in Hebrew alone
questions.explanation: Acts 2 records the disciples speaking in various languages by the Spirit's power, astonishing the diverse crowd gathered in Jerusalem for Pentecost.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Peter's sermon at Pentecost, recorded in Acts 2, resulted in
options: about three thousand people being baptised and added to the church in a single day
no response at all from the crowd
the complete rejection of the Gospel message
questions.explanation: Acts 2:41 records that around three thousand people responded to Peter's sermon and were baptised on the day of Pentecost.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The parable of the Sower describes seed falling on rocky ground as representing
options: those who receive the word with initial joy but fall away when trouble comes
those who produce the greatest harvest
those who never hear the word at all
those who deliberately reject the word from the start
questions.explanation: Matthew 13 explains that seed on rocky ground represents hearers who respond joyfully at first but lack the depth to endure trials.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the book of Romans, Paul teaches that a person is justified (made right with God) primarily through
options: strict observance of Jewish ceremonial law alone
faith, not by works of the law
questions.explanation: Romans presents Paul's central argument that justification comes through faith in Christ, not through obedience to the law.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: According to Paul's teaching in Romans, the purpose of the Law was mainly to
options: guarantee automatic righteousness for all who followed it
reveal humanity's sin and need for God's grace
replace the need for faith entirely
provide an alternative path to salvation apart from faith
questions.explanation: Paul argues in Romans that the Law exposes sin, showing humanity's need for the grace offered through faith in Christ.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Paul's teaching on grace in Romans emphasises that salvation is
options: an unearned gift from God, not something achieved through human effort
dependent on wealth or social standing
questions.explanation: Grace, as taught in Romans, is God's unmerited favour, freely given rather than earned through human works.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In 1 Corinthians 12, Paul teaches that spiritual gifts are given to believers mainly for
options: the common good and the building up of the whole Church
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12 emphasises that spiritual gifts, though varied, are given by the same Spirit for the benefit of the entire body of believers.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Paul's famous teaching on love in 1 Corinthians 13 emphasises that love is
options: unnecessary compared to prophecy and knowledge
patient, kind, and greater than even the most impressive spiritual gifts
a lesser virtue compared to faith and hope
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13 famously describes love's qualities and concludes that love is the greatest of all virtues, surpassing even prophecy, knowledge, and faith.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: According to Paul's teaching on civil authorities, found in passages such as Romans 13, Christians are generally instructed to
options: obey only religious leaders and no one else
submit to and respect governing authorities, since their power is established by God
rebel against all forms of government
questions.explanation: Romans 13 teaches that believers should generally respect and submit to civil authorities, recognising government as an institution permitted by God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In his teaching on Christian family relationships (as in Ephesians and Colossians), Paul instructs husbands to
options: love their wives as Christ loved the Church
avoid all responsibility within the household
treat their wives merely as servants
rule over their wives without any regard for their needs
questions.explanation: Ephesians 5:25 instructs husbands to love their wives sacrificially, following the model of Christ's love for the Church.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Paul's letters to Ephesians and Colossians also instruct children to
options: obey their parents in the Lord
questions.explanation: Ephesians 6:1 instructs children to obey their parents 'in the Lord', reflecting the importance of family order in Christian living.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The book of James teaches that genuine faith should be demonstrated through
options: words alone, without any accompanying action
avoidance of all trials and difficulties
questions.explanation: James famously teaches that 'faith without works is dead', emphasising that true faith naturally produces good works.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: According to the book of James, believers should respond to trials and difficulties with
options: joy, recognising that testing produces endurance and spiritual maturity
questions.explanation: James 1:2-4 encourages believers to consider trials as opportunities for joy, since they build perseverance and spiritual maturity.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The overall theme of Christian social responsibility, as taught across the Epistles, emphasises that believers should
options: focus solely on personal spiritual experiences
ignore the needs of others in their community
live out their faith practically in their relationships with others and society
questions.explanation: The Epistles consistently teach that genuine faith should be expressed through ethical living, love, and responsibility toward others in the wider community.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Paul's teaching in Romans regarding both Jews and Gentiles emphasises that
options: Jews and Gentiles must be saved through entirely different means
all people, Jew and Gentile alike, have sinned and are justified only through faith in Christ
questions.explanation: Romans emphasises the universal nature of sin and the equal access to salvation through faith, available to both Jews and Gentiles.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In 1 Corinthians 13, love is described as being superior even to which two other important spiritual qualities?
options: knowledge and prophecy alone, without mentioning faith or hope
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:13 concludes that of faith, hope, and love, the greatest of these three is love.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Paul's teaching that believers should not repay evil with evil, but rather live peaceably with others, reflects the broader New Testament emphasis on
questions.explanation: This teaching, found in passages such as Romans 12, reflects the broader New Testament call for believers to pursue peace and godly conduct even toward those who wrong them.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The book of James particularly warns believers against showing
options: favouritism toward the rich over the poor
questions.explanation: James 2 strongly criticises favouritism shown to wealthy members of the congregation at the expense of the poor, calling it inconsistent with genuine faith.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: According to the teaching found in Ephesians and Colossians, the overall pattern for right relationships within a household is one of
options: mutual submission, love, and respect among family members
domination of one family member over all others
total silence between husband and wife
complete independence with no mutual responsibility
questions.explanation: These epistles present household relationships as marked by mutual love, respect, and appropriately ordered submission, rather than domination.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Paul's overall purpose in writing to the Roman church was mainly to
options: explain in depth the Gospel of salvation by grace through faith
list the names of all the apostles
record the history of the early church in Jerusalem
give travel directions for his missionary journeys
questions.explanation: Romans is widely regarded as Paul's most systematic theological explanation of the Gospel, especially justification by faith.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The teaching that 'faith without works is dead' is most closely associated with the book of
questions.explanation: James 2:26 famously declares that faith without accompanying works is dead, emphasising the practical outworking of genuine faith.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Paul's teaching to the Corinthian church about spiritual gifts stresses that, despite their diversity, all gifts come from
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:4-11 emphasises that though spiritual gifts vary, they are all distributed by the same Spirit for the good of the Church.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The overarching lesson of the Epistles studied for CRS is that Christian doctrine (belief) should be matched by
options: practical Christian living and social responsibility
strict adherence to Old Testament ceremonial law alone
questions.explanation: A central thread running through the Epistles is that sound doctrine must be lived out through ethical conduct, love, and responsibility in daily life.
